Hi Li — great context, thanks.

Quick note: calendar clients display "local" time labels differently depending on timezone/DST settings. When someone in Sydney (UTC+10) receives an invite created in SGT (UTC+8) for 10:30 SGT, many clients will show the Sydney equivalent and append a "next day" marker if the offset crosses midnight in one of the participant's local zones. That looks like what happened.

Options:
- We can send a single invite with explicit timezone labels in the subject line (e.g., "10:30 SGT / 11:30 JST / 13:30 AEST").
- Or schedule two repeat-friendly slots that align to local working hours and let you choose (SGT morning or SYD afternoon).

Proposed concrete slots (I converted all to local zones for clarity):
- Tue Apr 20, 09:30 SGT / 10:30 JST / 12:30 AEST (45m)
- Tue Apr 20, 16:00 SGT / 17:00 JST / 19:00 AEST (45m) — note late for Tokyo but ok for Sydney

I'll attach the ICS we generate and include the explicit timezone text in the subject if you'd like. What works for Hiroshi + your Sydney folks?

Thanks,
Neha
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
